title: Practicum vs Internship: What's the Difference, and Do You Need Both?
summary: Practicum vs internship: which degrees require a practicum, the hours and supervision involved, credit, pay, and where each one goes on your resume.
body_markdown:
Practicum vs internship sounds like two names for one thing. It isn't. A practicum is a supervised placement your degree program requires, and you can't graduate without it. An internship is work experience you go out and get, and an employer runs it.


We sit down with a lot of students one-on-one, and in certain majors this mix-up comes up constantly. A social work or counseling student tells us they've "already done an internship," meaning the field placement their school arranged. Then they ask the real question. Do they still need one?


So this guide answers that with the accreditors' own rules for five fields, then shows where each experience goes on your resume.


## TL;DR


• A practicum is a supervised field placement that your degree program requires for academic credit. An internship is work experience you choose, run by an employer, and it may or may not come with credit or pay.


• Accreditors set practicum hours. Social work requires at least 400 field hours for a bachelor's degree and 900 for a master's, according to CSWE. Counseling requires a 100-hour practicum and then a 600-hour internship, according to CACREP.


• Most practicums are unpaid, and you pay tuition for the credits. Interns at the bachelor's level average $23.35 an hour, according to NACE, though some internships are unpaid too.


• A practicum counts toward your degree and, in licensure fields, toward the license. An internship doesn't.


• On a resume, a practicum goes under Education or Experience. An internship goes under Experience.


[Externships](https://www.extern.com/post/what-is-an-externship) are short, remote professional experience programs where you work on real projects with real companies. The projects are in business, tech, data and marketing, so they don't replace a practicum. If you'd like a look at a field outside your program, the[TruBridge Healthcare Data Analytics Externship](https://www.extern.com/externships/trubridge-healthcare-data-analytics-externship-oct-2026) , the[TikTok Social Media Content & Brand Strategy Externship](https://www.extern.com/externships/tiktok-social-media-content-brand-strategy-oct-2026) and the[Breaking Games E-Commerce Data Analysis & Strategy Externship](https://www.extern.com/externships/breaking-games-e-commerce-data-analysis-strategy-oct-2026) are open now.[Explore all Externships](https://www.extern.com/externships) .


---


## What Is the Difference Between a Practicum and an Internship?


The difference is who's in charge. Your school runs a practicum and an employer runs an internship, and the hours, supervision, credit and pay all follow from that.


### What Is a Practicum?


A **practicum** is a supervised field placement that a degree program requires for academic credit. Your school approves the site, a faculty member and a site supervisor share responsibility for you, and you log a set number of hours against written learning goals. In licensure fields, it's also a required step toward the license.


Programs call it different things: field education, fieldwork, field placement, student teaching, applied practice experience. The label changes. The structure doesn't.


### What Is an Internship?


An **internship** is a short, supervised work experience with an employer that lets you apply what you've studied and test a field.[NACE](https://naceweb.org/internships) describes it as experiential learning that connects classroom knowledge with practical application and skills development in a professional workplace.


It's usually optional. You find it and apply, the employer decides what you'll do, and it earns credit only if you arrange that with your school. We sort through the main formats in our guide to the[types of internships compared](https://www.extern.com/post/what-is-an-internship-types) .


### Practicum vs Internship at a Glance


Side by side, the two differ on almost every practical point: who requires it, who supervises you, whether anyone counts the hours and what ends up on your transcript.


Feature Practicum Internship


**Who requires it** Your degree program, and often the licensing path Usually nobody. You choose it


**Who arranges it** You and the school's field office. The school approves the site You apply, and the employer selects


**Supervision** A qualified site supervisor plus a faculty member, on a set schedule A manager at the employer. It varies


**Hours** Set by the program and its accreditor, logged and signed off Set by the employer. Often one summer or one semester


**Academic credit** Always. It is a course Only if you arrange it with your school


**Grade** Graded by faculty, often pass or fail No grade unless you take it for credit


**Pay** Usually unpaid, and you pay tuition for the credits Paid or unpaid. Bachelor's-level interns average $23.35 an hour (NACE, 2026)


**Counts toward a license** Yes, in licensure fields No


**Shows up in a background check** Documented by your school on your academic record Yes, the employer verifies it


**Resume section** Education or Experience Experience


---


## Which Degree Programs Require a Practicum?


Mostly the ones that lead to a license or a regulated job: social work, counseling, teaching, public health and psychology. Each field's accreditor writes the minimums, and your school builds on top of them.


### Social Work and Counseling


Social work has the clearest numbers. The Council on Social Work Education's[2022 accreditation standards](https://www.cswe.org/sites/default/files/2026-07/2022_EPAS.pdf) require at least 400 hours of field education for a bachelor's program and at least 900 for a master's. CSWE calls field education the "signature pedagogy" of social work.


Counseling is where the vocabulary gets confusing, because it uses both words. Under[CACREP's 2024 standards](https://www.cacrep.org/section-4-professional-practice/) , students first complete a practicum of at least 100 hours over a full academic term, with at least 40 of those hours in direct service with clients. Then comes an internship of 600 hours, with at least 240 in direct service.


So in a counseling program, practicum and internship aren't alternatives. They're stage one and stage two of the same requirement.


### Education, Public Health and Psychology


The other three fields follow the same logic under different labels:


• **Teacher education.** A practicum usually means the early classroom hours you complete before full-time student teaching. Each state sets its own rules. California's[credential program standards](https://docs.ctc.ca.gov/Document/Download/30447) , for example, require at least 600 hours of clinical practice across the program.


• **Public health.** Accredited MPH programs require an applied practice experience.[CEPH's guidance](https://media.ceph.org/documents/APE_basics.pdf) describes it by output: you show at least five competencies through at least two work products made for the host site. Your school's handbook sets the hours.


• **Psychology.**[APPIC](https://www.appic.org/About-APPIC/APPIC-Policies/DPA-Policy) , which runs the psychology internship match, asks the doctoral programs that join it to require practicum experience and a one-year, full-time internship (or two years half-time) of every student.


We can't give you one number that holds everywhere, because schools add to the minimums and rename things. Check your program handbook.


Wondering where one of these degrees leads? See our guides to[careers for psychology majors](https://www.extern.com/post/careers-for-psychology-majors-guide) and[what you can do with a public health degree](https://www.extern.com/post/public-health-degree-careers-guide) .


Field What programs require Who sets it


**Social work (bachelor's and master's)** At least 400 hours of field education for a bachelor's, 900 for a master's CSWE, 2022 standards


**Counseling (master's)** A 100-hour practicum, then a 600-hour internship CACREP, 2024 standards


**Teacher education** Early field hours, then student teaching. California requires at least 600 hours of clinical practice State licensing agencies


**Public health (MPH)** An applied practice experience: at least five competencies shown through two work products CEPH


**Psychology (doctoral)** Practicum experience and a one-year full-time internship APPIC membership criteria


### How Is a Practicum Different From a Clinical Placement?


**A clinical placement is a practicum where you work with patients.** Nursing, medicine, physical therapy and similar programs use "clinical placement" or "clinical rotation" for supervised hours with patients under a licensed preceptor. Practicum is the broader word, and it covers schools, agencies and health departments too.


Yet next to an internship, the two behave the same way: both are requirements with a sign-off, and you don't graduate without them. An internship usually isn't a graduation requirement, though a few majors do require one.


---


## How Do Supervision, Hours and Credit Work?


A practicum is supervised more tightly than almost any internship, and it's run like a course.


### Supervision and Required Hours


Practicum supervision is written into the standards, down to the minutes per week. In an internship, it depends on the manager you get.


Three examples from the accreditors:


• CACREP requires individual or triadic supervision averaging one hour a week, plus group supervision averaging an hour and a half a week, for the whole practicum.


• CACREP site supervisors need at least a master's degree and two years of professional experience after it.


• CSWE requires field supervisors to hold a social work degree from an accredited program, with at least two years of practice experience after earning it.


Your hours get logged, and someone signs them.


But an internship has none of that paperwork. That same NACE guide says an internship should have direct supervision by a professional, yet no outside body audits it.


### Academic Credit and Grading


A practicum is a course. You register for it, pay tuition for its credits and sign a learning agreement with your site. At the end, your site supervisor evaluates you and a faculty member assigns the grade, often pass or fail, depending on the school.


That has consequences. Fail it, or come up short on hours, and you may have to repeat the term. Graduation moves back with it.


And there's the part students resent, fairly: you're paying tuition to work without pay.


Internship credit runs the other way. Want credit? You ask your department, enroll in an internship course and usually write a report. Skip that step and the internship still happened. It just isn't on your transcript.


---


## Is a Practicum Paid?


Usually not. Most practicum placements are unpaid, and the reason is partly legal and partly about where they happen.


### Why Most Practicums Are Unpaid


Federal wage law allows unpaid placements when the student, not the organization, is the main beneficiary. The Department of Labor's[Fact Sheet #71](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/fact-sheets/71-flsa-internships) sets out a "primary beneficiary test" with seven factors for interns and students at for-profit employers. One factor is whether the placement is tied to your formal education through coursework or academic credit.


The setting matters too. Many placements are at schools, public agencies and nonprofits, and the same fact sheet notes that unpaid internships at public sector and nonprofit charitable organizations are generally permissible.


We said "usually," and there are exceptions. Some sites pay a stipend. The CSWE standards let each social work program decide whether you can complete field hours at an organization where you already work, as long as your field supervision stays separate from your job supervision. Already employed in the field? Ask.


None of this makes a semester of unpaid hours easy to afford. That's a real cost, and we won't pretend otherwise.


### How Internship Pay Compares


Internships are more likely to pay, but it isn't guaranteed. According to NACE's[2026 Guide to Compensation for Interns & Co-ops](https://naceweb.org/talent-acquisition/internships/hourly-wage-for-interns-climbs-but-is-down-over-last-10-years-in-real-terms) , interns at the bachelor's level earned an average of $23.35 an hour, based on what employers reported paying as of summer 2025.


Unpaid internships still exist, and they fall under the same primary beneficiary test. Our guide on[whether interns get paid](https://www.extern.com/post/do-you-get-paid-in-an-internship-guide) breaks pay down by industry.


---


## What If Your Program Requires a Practicum and You Also Want an Internship?


Do the practicum first, because it's the one you can't graduate without. Then decide whether an internship adds something the practicum doesn't.


### Can You Do Both?


Yes, usually in different terms. Here's the order we'd work in:


1. **Read your program handbook.** Find the total hours, which terms they fall in and how many hours a week the placement takes.


2. **Ask your field office what can count.** Some programs let a paid position or your current job count toward field hours. Many don't. Get the answer in writing.


3. **Fit the internship around the placement.** The academic calendar fixes your practicum dates, which makes a summer with no placement the easiest window. Our list of the[best websites to find internships](https://www.extern.com/post/best-websites-to-find-internships) covers where to look.


**Why add an internship:**


• **You pick the setting.** A practicum puts you where the program can place you.


• **It may pay.** That matters after a term of unpaid hours.


**Why you might not:**


• **Time.** Placement hours, classes and a job leave little room.


• **Your field may not ask for it.** Licensed professions hire on the degree, the supervised hours and the license.


### Adding Experience Outside Your Field


Sometimes the question isn't "more experience in my field." It's "what else could I do with this degree?" Picture an MPH student who keeps drifting toward the data.


A full-time internship is hard to fit beside a placement. Something remote and part-time is easier. An Externship is a remote professional experience built around a project and guided by an extern manager. Most run 8 weeks (the range is 4 to 11) at 5 to 10 hours a week, and the projects are in business, tech, data and marketing.


One thing to be clear about. An Externship isn't a clinical or licensure placement, so it can't replace a required practicum and it doesn't count toward licensure hours. It's a way to see a different field while your program covers your own.


At Extern, we've seen students use a short project to test a field outside their major. In our post-program survey (as of June 2026), the fields students most wanted to explore next were data analytics (21.1%), finance (19.6%) and artificial intelligence (18.7%). For a public health student, the[TruBridge Healthcare Data Analytics Externship](https://www.extern.com/externships/trubridge-healthcare-data-analytics-externship-oct-2026) is one example of what that looks like.


We compare other formats separately:[externship vs internship](https://www.extern.com/post/externship-vs-internship-guide) ,[co-op vs internship](https://www.extern.com/post/co-op-vs-internship-guide) and[apprenticeship vs internship](https://www.extern.com/post/apprenticeship-vs-internship-guide) .


---


## How Do You List a Practicum or Internship on a Resume?


Both belong on your resume. Where each one goes depends on who can confirm it.


### The Background Check Test


**Where does an experience go on a resume?** Ask one question: can it be confirmed in an employment background check? If an organization will verify your dates and your role, it belongs under Experience. If all you have is a certificate of completion, it belongs under Projects or Certifications.


A practicum is a special case. It usually isn't employment, so there may be no employer record of it.


But it's documented on your academic record, and your school can confirm it. That's why a practicum is usually listed under Education, or under Experience with the site named and the word "practicum" in the title. An internship is verified by the employer, so it goes under Experience. Externships on Extern support employment background checks.


Here's how each entry looks:


• **Practicum:** "School Counseling Practicum Student, Site Name, January to May 2026," with your hours and bullets on who you worked with and what you did under supervision. Or one line under your degree: "Field practicum, Site Name, 400 hours."


• **Internship:** "Program Intern, Employer Name, June to August 2026," with bullets on what you produced.


Don't retitle a practicum as a job. Our article on[resume claims and background checks](https://www.extern.com/post/lie-on-resume-background-check) explains what employers verify.


### How Recruiters Read Each One


We've spent years on the recruitment process outsourcing side, watching how employers screen candidates early in their careers. The two lines get read differently.


Inside your field, a practicum is expected. A hiring manager at an agency or a school already knows you did one, so they look at the setting, the population, the hours and who supervised you.


Outside your field, the word "practicum" may mean nothing to the reader. Translate it. "Conducted intake interviews and wrote case notes under weekly supervision" tells a recruiter more than "completed practicum requirements."


An internship reads as an employer picking you from a pool of applicants.


Either way, a vague line wastes the space. Our guide to[resume bullet points](https://www.extern.com/post/resume-bullet-points-guide) shows how to write a specific one. If you've completed an Externship, here's[how to list an Externship on your resume](https://www.extern.com/post/externship-on-resume-boosts-credibility) .


If you'd like a project in a different field to sit beside your practicum, you can[browse open Externships](https://www.extern.com/externships) .

## Frequently Asked Questions


### Is a practicum the same as an internship?


No. A practicum is a supervised placement that your degree program requires, approves and grades for credit. An internship is work experience you choose, and an employer runs it. Some fields use both words: under CACREP's 2024 standards, counseling programs require a 100-hour practicum first and a 600-hour internship after it.


### Do you get paid for a practicum?


Usually not. Most practicum placements are unpaid, and you pay tuition for the credits. There are exceptions. Some sites offer a stipend, and some social work programs allow a placement at the organization where you already work, if the program's policy permits it. Ask your field office before you assume either way.


### How many hours is a practicum?


It depends on the field and the accreditor. Social work programs must provide at least 400 hours of field education for a bachelor's degree and 900 for a master's, under CSWE's 2022 standards. Counseling programs require a 100-hour practicum followed by a 600-hour internship. Your program handbook lists the exact number.


### Does a practicum count as work experience?


It counts as supervised professional experience, and employers in your field expect to see it. It usually isn't employment, though, so there's often no employer record of it. Your school documents it on your academic record. List it under Education or under Experience with the site name, your role, dates and hours.


### Can you do a practicum and an internship at the same time?


Yes, if your schedule and your program allow it. The practicum comes first, because you can't graduate without it. A full-time internship on top of placement hours and classes is hard to sustain, so most students choose something part-time or remote, or wait for a term with no placement.
